topics.title: Introduction
objectives: Student can classify real numbers into rational and irrational categories
Student can identify terminating and non-terminating repeating decimals
visualIdeas: A tree diagram showing Real Numbers splitting into Rational and Irrational, with examples of each
A number line highlighting key positions for integers, fractions, and square roots

topics.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
objectives: Student can express any composite number as a product of its prime factors
Student can calculate the HCF and LCM of two positive integers using prime factorisation
Student can verify the relationship between HCF, LCM and the product of two numbers
visualIdeas: A factor tree for a composite number like 120 showing step-by-step factorization into prime nodes
A Venn diagram comparing prime factors of two numbers to find their HCF and LCM

topics.title: Revisiting Irrational Numbers
objectives: Student can prove the irrationality of square root of 2, 3, and 5 using proof by contradiction
Student can identify the sum or difference of a rational and an irrational number as irrational
visualIdeas: A step-by-step logic flowchart showing the contradiction assumption that root 2 equals p over q
A algebraic identity layout demonstrating why a rational multiplied by an irrational is irrational

topics.title: Introduction
objectives: Student can identify the degree of a given polynomial
Student can classify polynomials into linear, quadratic, and cubic based on their degrees
visualIdeas: A three-column layout presenting linear, quadratic, and cubic polynomials with their corresponding algebraic forms
A visual matching game linking algebraic expressions to their polynomial classification

topics.title: Geometrical Meaning of the Zeroes of a Polynomial
objectives: Student can locate the zeroes of a polynomial from its graphical representation
Student can state the relationship between the degree of a polynomial and the maximum number of zeroes it can have
visualIdeas: A 2D coordinate plane showing a parabola intersecting the x-axis at two distinct points, highlighted with bright circles
A series of graphs showing curves with 0, 1, 2, and 3 x-axis intersections to compare the count of zeroes

topics.title: Relationship between Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
objectives: Student can calculate the sum and product of zeroes of a quadratic polynomial using its coefficients
Student can construct a quadratic polynomial given the sum and product of its zeroes
visualIdeas: A side-by-side algebraic expansion matching the generic quadratic equation with the sum and product of alpha and beta
A worked solution table demonstrating the coefficient verification process for several quadratic examples

chapters.title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables

topics.title: Introduction
objectives: Student can represent a practical situation algebraically as a pair of linear equations
Student can identify the conditions for consistent, inconsistent, and dependent systems using ratio comparison
visualIdeas: A matrix of three scenarios comparing a1/a2, b1/b2, and c1/c2 to indicate intersection, parallelism, or coincidence
Two speech bubbles of real-life word problems showing their transformation into a pair of equations

topics.title: Graphical Method of Solution of a Pair of Linear Equations
objectives: Student can solve a pair of linear equations by plotting them on a coordinate grid
Student can identify the coordinates of the point of intersection of two plotted lines
visualIdeas: An animated coordinate grid where two lines are plotted point-by-point, meeting at a highlighted intersection
A visual table showing the coordinates of points that satisfy both equations simultaneously

topics.title: Substitution Method
objectives: Student can solve a pair of linear equations by substituting one variable in terms of the other
Student can check the solution by substituting the obtained values back into the original equations

A step-by-step algebraic column tracing the variable isolation process with highlighted substitutions

topics.title: Elimination Method
objectives: Student can solve a pair of linear equations by eliminating one variable using multiplication
Student can select the most appropriate variable to eliminate based on coefficient simplicity

A side-by-side comparison of eliminating x versus eliminating y to show which path requires fewer operations

topics.title: Introduction
objectives: Student can define a quadratic equation and write its standard form
Student can formulate a quadratic equation to represent a real-world scenario

A geometric diagram of a rectangular field showing how area leads to a quadratic equation

topics.title: Quadratic Equations
objectives: Student can verify whether a given equation is a quadratic equation by simplifying it
Student can distinguish a quadratic equation from linear or cubic equations

A classification chart sorting mixed algebraic equations into 'Quadratic' and 'Not Quadratic' bins

objectives: Student can solve a quadratic equation by splitting the middle term
Student can factorise quadratic trinomials to determine their real roots

Two bracketed factors equal to zero showing the splitting of the equation into two independent linear solutions

topics.title: Nature of Roots
objectives: Student can calculate the discriminant of a quadratic equation
Student can determine the nature of roots based on the sign of the discriminant

A visual graphic linking three different parabolas (intersecting twice, touching once, not touching) to the value of the discriminant

topics.title: Introduction
objectives: Student can identify patterns in a sequence of numbers to determine if they form an arithmetic progression

A list of numerical sequences with green checkmarks or red crosses indicating if they form an AP

objectives: Student can find the common difference of a given arithmetic progression

objectives: Student can locate points on a Cartesian coordinate plane
